mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months compresses discount rates for equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate accommodative monetary policy.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS has declined for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 5.5% for two consecutive months, it signals a deteriorating labor market that triggers equity sell-offs as corporate earnings face headwinds, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 45% of instances where UNRATE has exceeded 5.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in residential construction permits (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate revenue expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint increase in HOUST and RSAFS fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO < 100), supply chain disruptions and reduced manufacturing output lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate profits face pressure.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO is below 100.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year CPI inflation rate exceeds 2.5%, it signals persistent inflation that prompts the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors adjust for higher discount rates.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL YoY exceeds 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS < 1.0%) and high unemployment (UNRATE > 5.0%) indicates a stimulative monetary policy environment amid weak labor markets, which typically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as the market anticipates policy support.
regime_hint: stimulative policy with weak labor market
failure_condition: The joint condition of FEDFUNDS < 1.0% and UNRATE > 5.0% fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases, or the interaction term's Rank IC is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of slowing GDP growth (GDPC1 annualized growth rate < 1.5%), consumer and business confidence weakens, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as equity valuations adjust to lower growth expectations.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when GDPC1 annualized growth is below 1.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A rising trend in industrial production (INDPRO increasing for 3 consecutive months) indicates improving manufacturing activity, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where INDPRO has increased for 3 consecutive months.
